objective:
1. Train a lightweight model specifically for the multilevel solver. Teach it to correct the residual left after the coarse solve. The existing multilevel/CNN hybrid already reduced fluid-step time by about 25% on the matched 128³ test; its network was trained for a different correction process.
2. Reuse useful corrections between timesteps. Our GCR implementation currently discards its direction space after each pressure solve. Retaining a small useful subspace has precedent in pressure-Poisson solvers, and remains untested here.
3. Target the actual failure modes in training. Explicitly vary spatial wavelengths and rectangular geometry. On one failing rectangular case, 99.6% of pressure-error energy was in the lowest spatial modes.
4. Optimize inference and solver execution together. Channels-last alone saved about 12% on the matched 128³ test. Repeated operators, allocations and runtime exchange deserve profiling next.
scope: All four numbered objectives remain required; a negative experimental result does not establish an improvement.
